# Excerpts of grok --help (grok 1.0.62), selected by the options the S01 cells cite.
# Made with: rg -n -A3 over the help text for the options named in this file's cells.
44:          When resuming (`--resume` / `--continue`), create a new session ID instead of reusing the original (optionally set via `--session-id`)
45-
46-      --fullscreen
47-          Open in the standard fullscreen TUI for this session, overriding a config `[ui] screen_mode = "minimal"` preference. Session-scoped only, does not write config. Fullscreen-vs-inline still follows the alt-screen policy (--no-alt-screen, [terminal] alt_screen, terminal auto-detection)
--
53:          Emit incremental `stream_event` lines (text/thinking deltas) alongside whole messages. Only affects `--output-format streaming-messages-json`
54-
55-      --json-schema <SCHEMA>
56:          JSON Schema for structured output. When set, the model is constrained to produce JSON matching this schema. Implies --output-format json. Example: --json-schema '{"type":"object","properties":{"name":{"type":"string"}}}'
57-
58-      --leader-socket <PATH>
59-          Use a custom leader socket path instead of the default `~/.grok/leader.sock`. A local/branch build can thus run an isolated leader without colliding with the default one already running on the machine Name it `~/.grok/leader-*.sock` to keep `grok leader list/kill` able to find it; any other location works but won't be auto-discovered
--
82:      --output-format <OUTPUT_FORMAT>
83-          Output format for headless mode
84-
85-          Possible values:
--
96:      --permission-mode <MODE>
97-          Permission mode
98-          
99-          [possible values: default, acceptEdits, auto, dontAsk, bypassPermissions, plan]
--
107:  -r, --resume [<SESSION_ID_OR_TITLE>]
108-          Resume a session by ID or title, or the most recent if omitted. Non-ID values match session titles for the current directory, ignoring letter case; UUID-shaped values always mean IDs. Without an exact match, the same words joined by any separators also match: quote "fix login bug" or write fix-login-bug. Among duplicate titles a sole renamed match wins; otherwise the resume fails as ambiguous
109-
110-      --reasoning-effort <EFFORT>
--
122:          Use a specific session UUID for a **new** conversation (must be a valid UUID and must not already exist under the target session directory). With `--resume`/`--continue`, only valid together with `--fork-session` (names the forked session). Does not resume existing sessions, use `--resume` / `--continue` instead
123-
124-      --sandbox <PROFILE>
125-          Sandbox profile for filesystem and network access
--
132:      --tools <TOOLS>
133-          Built-in tools to allow (comma-separated)
134-
135-  -v, --version
--
142:          Start the session in a new git worktree, optionally named. With `--resume` of a remote session, pass `--restore-code` to apply the snapshot codebase (conversation is restored either way)
143-
144-      --worktree-ref <WORKTREE_REF>
145-          Branch, tag, or commit to base the worktree on (with `--worktree`). Defaults to the current HEAD of the source checkout when omitted
